title: Reproduce a sealed OLS decomposition on a bundled xy slice
goal: Fit the bundled 640-point slice assets/gc-387/data.csv with closed-form simple OLS and reproduce the sealed decomposition -- slope, intercept, SSE/SSR/SST, residual std with n-2 degrees of freedom, residual extremes, and a fixed-point prediction -- per assets/gc-387/spec.md, into artifacts/gc-387/stats.json. Before grading, validate intermediates with at least one independent cross-check (for example, confirm r_squared equals both 1 - SSE/SST and pearson_r squared, and SSR + SSE equals SST). Then run python3 assets/gc-387/grade.py and drive every named mismatch to zero across repeated verify cycles.
resources: assets/gc-387/data.csv (bundled dataset slice, sealed by sha256)
assets/gc-387/spec.md (exact statistic definitions and submission contract)
pypi:numpy==1.26.4 (optional, for the agent-side pipeline only)
pypi:pandas==2.2.2 (optional, for the agent-side pipeline only)
process_expectations: A plan artifact (e.g., plan.md) exists before any pipeline code and restates all 12 statistic definitions from spec.md in the agent's own words.
Intermediate self-verification commands ran, with captured output, before the first grader invocation.
The grader command was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run check and one final run -- and both stdout JSON lines are preserved in the run log.
Every RED grader run is followed by a log entry naming the mismatched statistics (identities, not counts) and the specific definition fix applied to each.
Cost and wall-clock are logged honestly per phase (plan / implement / verify), including failed attempts.

assets_visibility.note: sealed files live in the maintainers' private sealed pack; public repo keeps <name>.sha256 commitments. Restore with tools/restore_sealed.py before grading these cards.
